notes:
Account summary:
- Enterprise prospect evaluating Redwood Dedicated for regulated workloads (payments + internal ops tooling).
- Main theme across calls: "cost transparency" and the ability to break down $/1M output tokens by model + region + traffic class (prod vs sandbox) for finance/procurement.

Use case / workload notes:
- Current: internal agent for support + operations (summarization + Q&A over policy/docs), some lightweight embeddings-based retrieval.
- Traffic: expecting 200–500 concurrent chats during peak (business hours), plus batch summarization jobs overnight.
- Latency targets (stated): p50 < 700ms first token for chat in NA; p95 < 2.5s. For EMEA: willing to accept ~+200–400ms if residency is maintained.
- Model preferences: wants "best quality" model for complex cases, plus cheaper fallback for simple intents. Asked for guidance on routing policy and failover between regions.

Pricing / unit economics requirements (repeated):
- Procurement lead asked for a region/model breakdown (NA vs EU; primary model vs fallback) and how cache hit rate/batching impacts effective $/1M output tokens.
- Quote from meeting: "We need to explain variance to Finance by region and model family — a blended number isn’t enough unless we can drill down." 
- Asked whether Redwood can export monthly summary: output tokens, input tokens, and blended $/1M output tokens by (region, model, dedicated pool).
- Also asked for clarity on what’s included in "blended" (compute + overhead allocation) and whether credits/discounts affect reporting.

Security / compliance requirements:
- Must support VPC deployment for Dedicated; private connectivity preferred (PrivateLink / direct peering discussion).
- Requirements checklist from security questionnaire (in progress): SSO/SAML for Console, audit logs with 1yr retention (or export), KMS-backed encryption, role-based access controls, and data residency controls for EU traffic.
- Asked specifically about: 
  - audit log fields (who accessed what cost views / model configs)
  - data retention policy for prompts/outputs (they want default = no retention beyond operational needs)
  - access control around "discount-sensitive" views (procurement wants assurance only Finance/admin roles see certain cost details)

Procurement process notes:
- Vendor onboarding: need SOC 2 Type II report, insurance certificate, and standard DPA.
- Wants a redlined MSA review; legal timeline estimated 3–5 weeks after security sign-off.
- Billing: prefers invoicing by cost center with region-level rollups.

Recent activity timeline:
- 2025-01-17: Intro + discovery call. Key asks: Dedicated in VPC, cost by region/model, predictable throughput.
- 2025-01-29: Technical deep dive w/ SE. Discussed routing/fallback and telemetry. (Fireflies: ff-903182)
- 2025-02-05: Sent initial pricing ranges; procurement replied requesting itemized breakdown + reporting format.
- 2025-02-11: Follow-up call focused on security questionnaire and data residency controls; agreed to share SOC 2 + architecture diagrams.

Open questions (from prospect):
- Can Redwood provide region/model cost reporting aligned with their finance definitions (and exportable)?
- How do we ensure EU requests never fail over to NA (except explicit override), while still preserving service continuity?
- For Dedicated: how is GPU fleet cost allocated if they add a second region later? (wants clear policy)

Internal notes / Redwood follow-ups:
- We should position Redwood’s internal unit economics work as the mechanism to provide drilldowns + explainability (mix shift, cache hit-rate changes, routing changes).
- Need to confirm which cost views can be shared externally vs internal-only (esp. overhead allocation assumptions).
- SE to propose an initial routing policy: primary = EU region for EMEA tenants; fallback within EU first; explicit NA failover only if allowed.

Contacts (prospect side, partial):
- Head of Platform Engineering (technical evaluator)
- Procurement Manager (pricing + vendor onboarding)
- Security GRC (questionnaire owner)

Risks:
- Strong preference for cloud-native provider with built-in compliance documentation; if we’re slow on security artifacts, they’ll default to AWS/Azure.
- Without a credible cost drilldown/export story, Finance may block even if technical team likes performance.
